text: Argentina competed at the 2004 Summer Olympics in Athens, Greece, from 13 to 29 August 2004, marking its twenty-first appearance at the Olympic Games, with absences from the 1904 Summer Olympics in St. Louis, the 1912 Summer Olympics in Stockholm, and the 1980 Summer Olympics in Moscow due to support for the United States-led boycott. Carlos Espínola served as the nation's flag bearer at the opening ceremony. A total of 152 competitors—106 men and 46 women—participated in 86 events across 22 sports. Argentina's total medal count of six represented its best performance since the 1948 Summer Olympics, securing its first gold medals since 1952 and achieving its highest position in the medal table up to that point, placing 35th overall. Argentina qualified athletes in athletics events (up to three at the 'A' Standard and one at the 'B' Standard), qualifying a men's team, two competitors for the canoeing flatwater event, one fencer, nine judoka, and a team for the men's indoor tournament. The men's basketball roster, men's field hockey roster (headed by Jorge Ruiz), women's field hockey roster (headed by Sergio Vigil), men's football roster (headed by Marcelo Bielsa), and men's volleyball roster (headed by Alberto Armoa) were all officially listed. Argentina had one woman competing in artistic gymnastics as an individual. Swimmers earned qualifying standards in events with a maximum of two at the A-standard and one at the B-standard. Qualification results used the legend: Q = Qualify to final; q = Qualify to semifinal; FA = Final A (medal); FB = Final B (non-medal); FC = Final C (non-medal); FD = Final D (non-medal); FE = Final E (non-medal); FF = Final F (non-medal); SA/B = Semifinals A/B; SC/D = Semifinals C/D; SE/F = Semifinals E/F; R = Repechage. M = Medal race; OCS = On course side of the starting line; DSQ = Disqualified; DNF = Did not finish; DNS = Did not start; RDG = Redress given. One athlete was noted as over-aged.
